Subject: Private deploy residency — dependency matrix & authorization request (EU/APAC)

Hi Alex / Acme team,

Thanks again for the sync last week. Per our run-through, I'm sending the consolidated dependency matrix and a short ask list so we can lock the cutover window for the EU -> APAC private deployments. The attached spreadsheet (redwood-dep-matrix-v2.xlsx) maps each service, required network peering, BGP routes, KMS key usage, DNS delegation, and the minimum test gate for a regional failover.

Quick summary of what we need from Acme to proceed to scheduling:
- Confirmation of the cross-border KMS escrow process (see attached kms-escrow-instructions.pdf). We need whether you will accept Redwood-managed wrapped keys or prefer on-prem key unwrapping at cutover.
- Network: approval of the peering CIDR ranges and a maintenance window for the peering swap (BGP community tags are in column D).
- Compliance: a named approver from your Data Privacy / Legal team for the residency exception table (row 12 of the matrix).
- Ops: a single point-of-contact for the cutover execution (we've listed platform.ops@acme-retail.com but please confirm).

Proposed target window: 2026-07-15 02:00-06:00 UTC (low traffic in both EU and APAC). If that doesn't work, provide two alternates.

Notes and constraints from Redwood's side are inline in the matrix. The short list of non-negotiables:
- No plain-text KMS key export from EU region to APAC; any cross-region key movement must be wrapped and escrowed.
- Egress gating must remain active during the DNS propagation window; we will provide a temporary allowlist for the cutover.

Please review and reply with approvers and your preferred KMS option by EOD Wed (2026-06-24). If helpful, we can run a 30-min tabletop with your SRE + Security tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deploy residency — dependency matrix & authorization request (EU/APAC)

Thanks Sofia — reviewed the matrix. Two technical clarifications from infra: 

1) Failover ordering and routing weights: column F lists the preferred ordering (EU-primary, APAC-standby). For applications that cannot tolerate eventual consistency on session affinity, we'll set sticky-route overrides at the edge for 15 minutes post-switchover; this is explicit in the gating checks but worth highlighting for Acme.

2) KMS: we recommend option B (Redwood wraps a per-customer ephemeral key, escrow the wrapped envelope to your legal custodian). This avoids any HSM cross-region export and keeps us within your residency constraints. If Acme insists on unwrapping on-prem, we need the on-prem key-unwrapping play documented and validated in the tabletop.

3) BGP communities: I'll add the exact community tags for the planned failover path tonight. Also flagging that private-link health checks will need a /31 NAT on your side for the probe IPs — noted in matrix row 8.

If Acme confirms the wrapped-key approach, we can auto-schedule a dry-run two weeks before the cutover.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood
From: Alex Chen <sre.acme@acme-retail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 06:58:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy residency — dependency matrix & authorization request (EU/APAC)

Sofia / Karthik,

Appreciate the matrix — useful level of detail. A few follow-ups from our end after a quick internal review:
- KMS: Acme legal leans toward on-prem unwrapping for long-term auditability. However, for the first opt-in run we are open to the wrapped-escrow flow if Redwood provides a notarized audit record of the wrapping keys (or a signed KMS-transaction log). Can your team provide signed transaction logs or HSM proofs?
- Peering/Routes: The proposed maintenance window looks reasonable. We need you to confirm rollback criteria (latency thresholds, 5xx spike thresholds, and packet-loss thresholds). Put numeric gates in the runbook and we'll confirm.
- DNS: Our DNS TTLs are 300s but the internal caching in APAC gateways is noisy. We request a temporary dual-write period of 10 minutes where both EU and APAC are writable for non-sensitive metadata only; is that acceptable?

We'll tag our SRE PO (platform.ops) to coordinate the BGP prep. Legal (copied) — can you confirm a named approver and whether the wrapped-escrow logs meet your audit bar?

Thanks,
Alex
SRE Lead, Acme Retail

Hi Legal / Jordan,

Forwarding the thread and the matrix. Acme is okay to accept the wrapped-key escrow for an initial dry-run if we can provide signed HSM transaction logs and a short addendum that documents the escrow custody chain. We need a named approver from Redwood's side to sign the addendum and a short exec-level signoff that allows the temporary reserved capacity billing to proceed.

Can you: 1) confirm whether the wrapped-key logs are sufficient evidence for our SOC2 auditors, and 2) provide a named signatory for the addendum (ideally VP-level or above) so Acme can route for approval?

Executive summary for approval (one-pager pasted below):
- Purpose: Controlled cutover for private deployment residency between EU (primary) and APAC (standby).
- Key risk: accidental unencrypted cross-border key export. Mitigation: wrapped-key escrow with legal custodian + signed HSM transaction logs.
- Operational gates: BGP and health-check thresholds; DNS dual-write period; temporary reserved capacity for APAC.
- Ask: VP-level sign-off on addendum + authorization to bill temporary capacity.

Thanks — need this by EOD so we can lock the dry-run date.

Sofia
